'''''Crepis vesicaria''''' is a [[Europe]]an species of flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]] with the common name '''beaked hawk's-beard'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref name=gerta>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=crepis+vesicaria Altervista Flora Italiana, Radicchiella rosea, Beaked hawksbeard, Löwenzahn-Pippau, blåsfibbla, ''Crepis vesicaria'' L.] includes photos and European distribution map</ref> It is native to the Western and Southern [[Europe]] from [[Ireland]] and [[Portugal]] east as far as [[Germany]], [[Austria]], and [[Greece]].<ref name=gerta/> It became naturalized in scattered locations in [[North America]].<ref name=gerta/><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Crepis%20vesicaria.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref>

''Crepis vesicaria''  is an [[Annual plant|annual]], [[Biennial plant|biennial]], or [[Perennial plant|perennial]] herb up to 120 cm (48 inches or 4 feet) tall, producing a large underground [[caudex]]. Each plant can have as many as 20 [[flower heads]], each with up to 70 [[ray florets]] but no [[disc floret]]s. It grows on hillsides and in sandy clearings.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066455 Flora of North America, Beaked hawksbeard ''Crepis vesicaria'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 805. 1753.]</ref>

A prominent plant, Crepis vesicaria stands erect, with many  branches, each ending in its own dandelion-like flower.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=A flora of California, by Willis Linn Jepson.|last=Jepson|first=Willis Linn|date=1909|publisher=Cunningham, Curtis & Welch|location=San Francisco, Calif.|doi = 10.5962/bhl.title.7604|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/32007}}</ref>

The underside of the flower has two layers of leaf-like [[phyllary|phyllaries]]. The inner layer is longer and pointed, and often curls back away from the rest of the flower head. The outer layer is substantially shorter.<ref name=":0" />

The plant is a source of [[helenynolic acid]], a rare fatty acid.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Spencer |first1=G. F. |last2=Earle |first2=F. R. |last3=Wolff |first3=I. A. |last4=Tallent |first4=W. H. |title=Oxygenation of unsaturated fatty acids in seeds during storage |journal=Chemistry and Physics of Lipids |date=1 February 1973 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=191–202 |doi=10.1016/0009-3084(73)90016-9 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0009308473900169?via%3Dihub |access-date=10 April 2025 |issn=0009-3084|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
